twfeweights: Implicit Weights and Covariate Balance for Difference-in-Differences Estimators

Source: R/imports.R
twfeweights-package.Rd

Computes the implicit weights that two-way fixed effects (TWFE) regressions and other difference-in-differences estimators place on group-time average treatment effects in staggered treatment adoption designs. Without covariates, the package recovers the weights that a TWFE regression places on each group-time average treatment effect (including pre-treatment periods), following de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2020) doi:10.1257/aer.20181169 and Goodman-Bacon (2021) doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2021.03.014 , and compares them with the weights behind the overall average treatment effect parameters in Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.12.001 . With covariates, it writes TWFE regressions and augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW), regression adjustment and inverse probability weighting estimators as reweighting estimators and reports how well the implied weights balance covariates across treated and comparison groups, as in Caetano and Callaway (2024) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2406.15288 .

Details

The package has three groups of functions.

Staggered adoption without covariates. twfe_weights() recovers the weights that a TWFE regression places on each group-time average treatment effect, \(ATT(g,t)\), estimated by did::att_gt(). attO_weights() and att_simple_weights() give the weights behind the overall average treatment effects of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021), for comparison.

Covariates, two periods. two_period_reg_weights() writes a TWFE regression with covariates as a reweighting estimator; two_period_aipw_weights() does the same for AIPW, regression adjustment and inverse probability weighting. Both report how well the implicit weights balance covariates.

Covariates, staggered adoption. implicit_twfe_weights() and implicit_aipw_weights() extend these to many periods; twfe_cov_bal() and aipw_cov_bal() compute covariate balance.

ggtwfeweights() plots the results. pooled_sd(), log_ratio_sd(), frac_treated_extreme() and effective_sample_size() compute the balance statistics and can be applied to any set of weights.

See vignette("twfe-weights", package = "twfeweights") and vignette("covariate-balance", package = "twfeweights").

References

Caetano, Carolina and Brantly Callaway. "Difference-in-Differences when Parallel Trends Holds Conditional on Covariates." Working paper (2024). doi:10.48550/arXiv.2406.15288

Callaway, Brantly and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna. "Difference-in-Differences with Multiple Time Periods." Journal of Econometrics 225.2 (2021). doi:10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.12.001
